(10 May 2017) | longest wins = [[El-Kanemi Warriors F.C.|El Kanemi Warriors]] (4) | longest unbeaten = [[Plateau United F.C.|Plateau United]] (7) | longest winless = [[Remo Stars F.C.|Remo Stars]] (14) | longest losses = [[Kano Pillars F.C.|Kano Pillars]] (4) | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = 2,556 | prevseason = [[2016 Nigeria Professional Football League|2016]] | nextseason = [[2018 Nigeria Professional Football League|2018]] | updated = 20 September 2017 }} The '''2017 Nigeria Professional Football League''' was the 46th season of the top Nigerian professional league for association football clubs, since its establishment in 1972, and the 27th since the rebranding of the league as the "Professional League". [[Plateau United]] won the league on the Saturday, 9 September 2017 with a 2-0 victory over [[Enugu Rangers]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2017/09/breaking-plateau-united-wins-20162017-npfl-title/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Plateau United wins Nigerian Professional Football League|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}} [[Enugu Rangers]] won [[2016 Nigeria Professional Football League|the previous edition]], their seventh league title and first since 1984. [[Plateau United]]'s win of this edition is their first ever title, which came in their second season after being promoted to the top flight. It was intended to be rational, meaning ''in reserve'' purposes. ==Clubs== A total of 20 teams contested the league, these included 16 teams from the [[2016 Nigeria Professional Football League|previous season]] and four teams promoted from the [[Nigeria National League]].
